content:
AIYANA BROOKS-TAN
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN / PORTFOLIO]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Computing student with hands-on experience building web applications using React and TypeScript, including an internship focused on accessibility and a full-stack academic project using Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL. Interested in creating accessible, user-focused web experiences. Experience also includes teaching support for first-year web development students.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, Tailwind CSS
Backend and data: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Firebase Authentication
Testing and documentation: Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook
Other: Chart.js, Vercel

EXPERIENCE
Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media | May 2024 – August 2024
- Worked on accessibility fixes and components for a React news site.
- Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages and documented it in Storybook.
- Used React, Storybook, Jest and React Testing Library.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
- Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development lab sessions.

Freelance Web Developer | 2025
- Built a yoga studio website with marketing pages and a class timetable; booking requests were sent by email.
- Used Next.js static generation and Tailwind CSS, with content managed in Markdown files; deployed on Vercel.

Part-Time Barista | Throughout college
- Worked part-time alongside college studies.

PROJECTS
Tidewatch | Final Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app for sea swimmers showing tides, water temperature and weather around the Irish coast.
- Developed the frontend with React and TypeScript and an API with Node.js and Express, caching data from public weather and tide APIs.
- Used PostgreSQL to store user favourites; used Chart.js for visualisations and Jest for testing.
- Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Awarded 82% (First Class) and demonstrated the project at the college project showcase.

Transit Delay Notifier | Student Hackathon | 2024
- Worked in a three-person team to build a transit delay notifier in 24 hours; developed the frontend.
- Placed second in the student hackathon.

Study Buddy | Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a web app matching classmates for study sessions as part of a four-person team.
- Used React, JavaScript and Firebase Authentication; other team members developed the API and database.

VOLUNTEERING
Social Media Volunteer | Sea Swimming Club
- Run social media for a sea swimming club.

EDUCATION
Computing | Liffey Institute of Technology

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, and professionally focused on React, TypeScript, accessibility, and full-stack academic work. The strongest evidence is specific and credible: the accessible gallery, Tidewatch project, screen-reader testing, Lighthouse score of 100, Storybook documentation, and hackathon result. The main content weaknesses are incomplete contact details, limited detail in some experience entries, an incomplete education entry, and insufficient separation between professional experience and student or freelance work. The barista role adds little for this target role and occupies space that could be used for more relevant evidence.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The conventional section headings, reverse-chronological structure, plain text formatting, and technology keywords should parse well in ATS software. Relevant terms include React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js, Storybook, accessibility, and Firebase Authentication. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior or graduate full-stack roles, but lower for this specific vacancy because the CV does not demonstrate the required 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, or web security fundamentals. The contact placeholders are a practical ATS and recruiter-readiness problem. Do not add unsupported keywords such as NestJS, Playwright, Docker, AWS, OWASP, GDPR, or healthcare data experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with Verdane Care's accessibility and patient-focused values. The Tidewatch application demonstrates accessible, user-focused web development, React/TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, API integration, visualisation, and automated testing. The yoga studio project provides relevant wellness-domain and Next.js experience, while the teaching assistant role supports the mentoring aspect of the position. Storybook is also a direct nice-to-have match. However, the candidate's material indicates only a four-month internship plus freelance and academic work, not the required 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience. The CV also does not establish end-to-end testing, Git workflows, OWASP or broader web-security awareness, semantic HTML, responsive-layout knowledge, health-data privacy experience, AWS/Docker, analytics/A-B testing, or German/Croatian. These are candidate-profile gaps or unsupported areas rather than defects that can be solved by inserting keywords.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the header, replace “[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN / PORTFOLIO]” with the candidate’s actual email address, phone number, and LinkedIn or portfolio URL. Do not submit the CV with placeholders.

2. In the Professional Summary, make the experience level more precise so the document does not imply extensive professional full-stack experience. For example, change the opening to: “Computing graduate/student with a software development internship and hands-on academic and freelance experience building web applications with React and TypeScript.” Retain the accessibility, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, and teaching-support evidence because those claims are supported.

3. In the Experience section under “Freelance Web Developer,” specify the scope accurately and make the relevant technical contribution easier to scan. For example, use: “Built and deployed a yoga studio website with marketing pages, a class timetable, and email-based booking requests using Next.js static generation, Tailwind CSS, Markdown content, and Vercel.” Do not describe this as a production booking system or imply payment/calendar integration.

4. In the Education section, complete the existing entry with the actual qualification title and dates if they are available in the candidate’s records. The current “Computing | Liffey Institute of Technology” entry is too incomplete for a graduate-level application. Do not invent a degree title, graduation date, or classification.

5. In the Skills section, make the evidence boundary clearer by grouping technologies that are demonstrated in projects versus technologies listed without accompanying project detail. For example, retain React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Firebase Authentication, Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Chart.js, and Vercel, but ensure each is supported by the Experience or Projects sections. Do not add Git, Playwright, OWASP, Docker, AWS, NestJS, or GDPR because they are not present in the original candidate information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
6. In the Software Development Intern entry, make the accessibility and testing evidence more prominent by combining the existing bullets into outcome-focused wording such as: “Built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages using React; documented the component in Storybook and used Jest and React Testing Library.” This remains faithful to the portfolio information and uses terms relevant to the vacancy.

7. In the Tidewatch project, retain the exact evidence that most closely matches the role: “React and TypeScript frontend,” “Node.js and Express API,” “PostgreSQL,” “Jest,” “NVDA and VoiceOver,” and “Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.” If space allows, label the section as “Selected Projects” and put Tidewatch first, since it is the strongest match.

8. In the Teaching Assistant entry, clarify the mentoring contribution without overstating it: “Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development lab sessions.” This is already supported and should remain concise.

9. Reduce the Part-Time Barista entry to a single line or remove it if space is needed for technical evidence. If retained, place it under a brief “Additional Experience” section rather than giving it equal visual weight with software roles. Do not use it to imply professional engineering experience.
critique.critical_issues:
1. The header contains unresolved placeholders for essential contact information: “[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN / PORTFOLIO].” This can prevent recruiter contact and reduce application-readiness.
2. The Professional Summary could be read as presenting the candidate as an experienced full-stack professional, although the original candidate information states there is no backend job experience and the professional internship lasted from May to August 2024. The wording should distinguish internship, freelance, academic, and project experience.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured early-career CV with strong evidence of React, TypeScript, accessibility, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, testing, and project delivery. The strongest material is specific and credible: the accessible gallery, NVDA and VoiceOver testing, Lighthouse score of 100, Tidewatch grade, and hackathon result. The main content weakness is that some bullets are descriptive rather than impact-oriented, and several role-relevant concepts are present only indirectly. The CV also needs to distinguish more clearly between professional experience, freelance work, academic projects, and teaching experience so the level of professional experience is immediately understood.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, readable bullets, and ATS-friendly technology names. It should parse well and has a moderate-to-high screening probability for junior React/TypeScript or junior full-stack roles. Relevant keywords include React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js, Storybook, accessibility, screen readers, and Firebase Authentication. Screening probability for this specific role will be reduced by the absence of explicit evidence for 2+ years of professional experience, Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, OWASP/web-security awareness, and privacy requirements. Those are candidate-experience gaps or unsupported areas rather than wording defects. The phrase "Demonstrated in Experience and Projects" is understandable but less standard than a conventional skills taxonomy.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with Verdane Care's accessibility and patient-focused product context. Tidewatch demonstrates an accessible, data-driven web application with a React/TypeScript frontend, Node.js/Express backend, PostgreSQL storage, API integration, automated unit testing, screen-reader testing, and performance/accessibility validation. The yoga studio project provides relevant wellness-domain and Next.js experience, while the accessible gallery supports the Storybook nice-to-have. The CV does not meet or demonstrate the advertised 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience; the original material specifically says there is no backend job experience and describes backend work as project-based. It also does not demonstrate end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, OWASP/web-security awareness beyond authentication, German or Croatian, AWS/Docker, or analytics/A/B testing. English is demonstrated by the fluent English-language application material. The document shows wellness-related experience through the yoga studio website but not healthcare or regulated-environment experience. Overall, it is a credible junior-level technical match with particularly good accessibility alignment, but not a full match for the stated experience level.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the broad phrase "hands-on academic and freelance experience building web applications" with a more precise statement that separates professional and project experience, such as: "Computing student with a software development internship and freelance, academic, and hackathon experience building web applications with React and TypeScript." This accurately prevents the reader from interpreting the projects as two years of professional experience.

2. In the Technical Skills section, replace the category "Testing and documentation" with more ATS-specific categories and make supported accessibility evidence explicit. For example: "Testing: Jest, React Testing Library, Lighthouse"; "Accessibility: keyboard navigation, screen-reader testing, NVDA, VoiceOver"; and "Component documentation: Storybook." Do not add end-to-end testing tools or Git because they are not supported by the candidate material.

3. In the Tidewatch project, revise the second and third bullets to use the job description's terminology more directly while remaining truthful. For example: "Developed a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js/Express backend service, caching data from public weather and tide APIs" and "Used PostgreSQL as the SQL database for user favourites and Jest for unit testing." This makes the full-stack, backend-service, SQL-database, and unit-testing evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.

4. In the Tidewatch project, make the accessibility and performance evidence more searchable by revising the fourth bullet to: "Performed accessibility testing with NVDA and VoiceOver and achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100." If semantic HTML or responsive layouts were actually part of the project, they may be named here only if they are accurate; do not add them based on the job description alone.

5. In the Study Buddy project, revise the final bullet to state the supported security-related experience more precisely: "Built login screens and integrated Firebase Authentication for user sign-in; other team members developed the API and database." This highlights authentication without implying broader OWASP or application-security experience.

6. In the Software Development Intern entry, revise the first bullet to combine the accessibility work and frontend technology into a stronger, keyword-rich achievement: "Implemented accessibility fixes and React components for a news website, including keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly article experiences." Keep the existing Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library evidence in the following bullet.

7. In the Freelance Web Developer entry, change "email-based booking requests" to "email-based class booking requests" and retain "Next.js static generation, Tailwind CSS, Markdown content, and Vercel". This makes the wellness-domain relevance clearer without suggesting healthcare or patient-booking experience.

8. In the Teaching Assistant entry, make the mentoring evidence more explicit by changing the bullet to: "Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development lab sessions, answering questions and helping them troubleshoot web-development work." Only retain the troubleshooting wording if it accurately reflects the work performed; otherwise keep the current factual wording.
